ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The AC generator at the power plant outputs a constant voltage of $200\mathrm{V}$ and a power of $100\mathrm{kW}$. The electricity needs to be transmitted to a distant factory. The designed power loss on the transmission line is $10\%$, and the total resistance of the transmission line is $100\Omega$.

1. What is the current on the transmission line?
2. What is the turns ratio of the step-up transformer required for power transmission (assuming the transformer used is an ideal transformer)?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The AC generator at the power plant outputs a constant voltage of $200\mathrm{V}$ and a power of $100\mathrm{kW}$. The electricity needs to be transmitted to a distant factory. The designed power loss on the transmission line is $10\%$, and the total resistance of the transmission line is $100\Omega$. 1. What is the current on the transmission line? 2. What is the turns ratio of the step-up transformer required for power transmission (assuming the transformer used is an ideal transformer)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the text: generator voltage V1 = 200 V, generator power P = 100 kW = 100000 W, designed line loss is 10%, and total line resistance R = 100 Ω. The allowed transmission-line loss is P_loss = 0.10 × 100 kW = 10 kW = 10000 W. Using Joule heating loss on the line, P_loss = I^2 R, so I = sqrt(P_loss/R) = sqrt(10000/100) = sqrt(100) = 10 A. For an ideal step-up transformer, the transmission side receives the generator power, so the required transmission voltage is V2 = P/I = 100000 W / 10 A = 10000 V. The transformer turns ratio equals the voltage ratio: N1:N2 = V1:V2 = 200:10000 = 1:50.
